title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; reported inferential statements apply only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. Such pipelines demonstrably reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, simple ordering and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs, avoiding confounding from independent per-condition generation. Our principal contribution is a concrete, artifact-grounded quantification of that marginal verifier-detected improvement (and its statistical bounds) for a constrained NetOps task bank.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical studies have shown active interest in LLMs for intent-driven network configuration and in architectures that layer deterministic checks over stochastic generation [1],[2],[4]. Prior NetOps-focused evaluations report LLMs generating plausible draft configurations under emulation or constrained corpora, but they also emphasize the need for verification due to syntax/policy failure modes [1],[5]. Deterministic verification tools and model-checking approaches (e.g., Batfish evolution and header-space techniques) are mature for mechanized checks (reachability, forwarding, local-policy) and are used as validators in GVR pipelines [4],[6].

Program-repair and generate–verify workflows in code and configuration domains provide precedent for bounded automated repair improving mechanical correctness [3]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats underline that filtering and validator stages are necessary for hardening LLM-integrated pipelines, though adaptive adversaries remain an open evaluation challenge [7].

This study differs from prior work by (i) using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) reporting deterministic provider-call accounting and stage counts that reconcile shared initial generations with the single permitted repair, and (iii) archiving full validator traces and reconciliation artifacts for auditability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1. The confirmatory design specified N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, a single permitted automated repair per episode, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary pass/fail outcomes, supplemented by a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede. All analysis code, manifests, and analytic parameters were fixed before observing outcomes.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution accounting. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one initial model generation was produced per intent; that same generated candidate was reused for both baseline and guarded episodes for the pair. The adapter-level provider audit reconciles hosted_model_call_event_count = 251, stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}. These stage mappings explain why the adapter reports 251 model-call events despite two episodes per pair: one shared initial-generation call per pair (reused) plus at most one repair-stage generation in a guarded episode. This reconciliation is key to correctly interpreting model-call accounting under shared candidate semantics.

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intents. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, workflow policies (make-before-break, all-down-before-change patterns), and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks intentionally exercised operational-like dependency rules (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired MTU changes) while constraining ambiguity by enumerating allowed_touched_fields and required_sequence; representative task payloads are archived with the execution manifest.

Model, validator, and repair policy. The declared model for initial generations was gpt-5-mini. For each intent we executed one shared initial generation. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, enforcing required_sequence ordering, checking workflow constraints, computing a final_state snapshot, and returning a boolean valid flag and violation codes. If valid = false the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair and re-submitted the repaired candidate to the validator. Repair templates were limited to deterministic syntactic and ordering adjustments (reordering commands, splitting/joining command lines, correcting token ordering) and did not permit multi-iteration free-form repair or human escalation.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. The pre-registered exclusions removed items that deterministically prevented verification (vendor-parser failures) or that matched denylist/credential patterns. Contamination detectors flagged embedded instruction-like tokens or private-address artifacts; flagged items would be excluded from the primary analysis and examined in sensitivity checks. For this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged; complete_pair_count = 250.

Analysis. The primary confirmatory analysis was implemented by the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1: exact McNemar two-sided test for the paired contingency (n10, n01) and a paired-bootstrap percentile CI for the guarded − baseline difference (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary descriptive analyses (per-difficulty diagnostics, parsed_command_count summaries, repair-conversion fraction) were run as exploratory checks.
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. Execution completed all planned episodes: planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250. Model-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}). No episodes met preregistered exclusion criteria; contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes.

Primary binary outcomes. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair corresponds to the only exercised repair call; that repair converted the failing baseline candidate to a guarded pass. The repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These precise numeric outputs and the bootstrap parameters are archived with the analysis artifacts.

Validator diagnostics and representative artifacts. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count enumerated by the task payload's required_sequence. Representative task artifacts (for example, a hard difficulty task with parsed_command_count = required_command_count = 6) and the raw shared candidate strings are archived; validator traces include normalized_configuration, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and the final_state snapshot used for intent-satisfaction checks.

Repairs exercised. Only one automated repair was invoked in this confirmatory run; its trace shows a deterministic reordering fix that satisfied the validator on recheck. No other repair calls occurred.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of a near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the lone failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) is the primary inferential statement: within the executed task scope and under shared-candidate semantics, the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement is small.

Artifact-grounded reasons for the small observed gain. (1) The task generator encoded constrained intents, explicit allowed_touched_fields, and exact required_sequences that reduce ambiguity and bias outputs toward well-formed CLI sequences. (2) The declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents. (3) The deterministic validator checked mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshot) and therefore would not detect higher-order semantic flaws not captured by the validator encoding.

Power and preregistered assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect at ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) substantially exceeded that assumption, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements; consequently, the confidence interval bound is the more informative operational summary for this experimental scope.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, single-repair policy, and shared_initial_candidate semantics; alternative generation semantics or multiple repairs could change outcomes. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable intent satisfaction (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) but does not measure live protocol dynamics or emergent cross-device behaviors. External validity: the confirmatory evidence applies only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory. Security validity: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised.

Operational implications (bounded). In tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM, the marginal validator-detected improvement from a single repair may be small; this does not imply validators are unnecessary in broader or adversarial settings. Validators that encode broader device/vendor behaviors, multi-iteration repairs, human escalation, or richer external tests may produce substantially different operational benefits. Production heterogeneity and adversaries remain unresolved risks.

Reproducibility. All run artifacts (raw shared responses, execution manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis outputs) are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement. Key numeric reconciliation facts reported above (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}; contingency counts n11=249/n10=1/n01=0/n00=0; bootstrap parameters) are reproducible from those artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory comparison was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived and available in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and conducted pre-lock infrastructure development; no manual post-lock manuscript technical edits were performed.

Models, tools, and manifest pointer: Declared generation model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The full archived evidence bundle (execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, provider-call audit, and per-artifact hashes) is available under the run manifest root execution/execution_manifest.json in the archived repository referenced by the submission evidence bundle. Preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede. Immutable master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Preregistered/actual estimand and deviation: The preregistration specified multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the executed confirmatory estimand reported in this manuscript is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Provider-call accounting in the archive reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) and stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Autonomy and reproducibility procedures: The preregistration, execution manifests, raw outputs, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts (including the contingency table and bootstrap parameters) are archived in the evidence bundle and referenced by the manifest root above to permit independent verification of the numeric claims in this paper.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.
Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected final_state) but did not measure live protocol-level correctness or emergent cross-device behaviors.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adaptive prompt-injection, retrieval-based attacks, and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
The realized baseline pass-rate (0.996) departed from the preregistered power assumption (~0.90), reducing power to detect small absolute paired improvements.
